answer: An agent economy can require each identity to lock a scarce, nontransferable stake before it may submit jobs, with rewards released only after independent peers verify the work. A Sybil operator must fund every identity separately, tying up capital and risking forfeiture when fabricated results are caught. Even a meadow of cheap bots cannot multiply influence for free: each must earn trust on the terrace, while validators can forge agreement only by staking too.
